title: Working at Redwood: roles, career ladders, benefits, hiring & onboarding, internal tools
author: Ava Chen
content:
Overview

This document is the canonical Company Handbook entry for new and existing Redwood employees. It covers: what it means to work at Redwood; role families and career ladders; benefits and perks; a high-level hiring and new-hire onboarding overview; and key internal tools and access patterns. Use this page as the first-stop reference for People Ops, managers, and new hires.

Purpose and scope

- Purpose: Provide a single, maintained reference that standardizes expectations across teams and supports consistent hiring, leveling, and onboarding.
- Scope: Applies to all Redwood employees and contractors who will be employed for more than 30 days. For team-specific variations (comp, schedules, on-call responsibilities), see the team-level playbooks linked in Related pages.

Company values and ways of working

- Build for the long term: prioritize reliability, observability, and cost-aware performance in our product and operations.
- Developer-first mindset: we prioritize predictable platforms, strong documentation, and fast onboarding.
- Collaboration and ownership: teams share responsibility for reliability, security, and customer outcomes.
- Inclusive and remote-friendly: default to inclusive communication and async-first collaboration.

Roles & career ladders (overview)

This section summarizes the primary role families and ladder expectations. Each family has a detailed ladder doc with examples and interview rubrics (see Related pages).

1) Engineering (Backend, Runtime, Infra)
- Levels: IC1 / IC2 / IC3 / Senior IC / Staff / Principal
- Core expectations by level (summary):
  - IC1: learns codebase, delivers tasks with guidance, follows team conventions.
  - IC2: independently owns features, writes tests, participates in design discussions.
  - IC3: owns medium-sized services or features end-to-end; mentors junior engineers.
  - Senior IC: leads significant subsystems, shapes architecture, drives on-call improvements.
  - Staff / Principal: cross-team technical leadership, sets platform strategy, large-scale impact.

2) Product & Design
- Levels: Associate PM / PM / Senior PM / Lead PM / Group PM (and parallel design ladder)
- Focus: customer outcomes, product strategy, roadmaps, cross-functional leadership.

3) SRE / Reliability / Ops
- Levels: Ops Engineer / SRE / Senior SRE / Staff SRE
- Expectations: define SLOs, own runbooks, capacity planning, incident leadership.

4) Applied ML & Research Ops
- Levels: Research Engineer / Applied ML Engineer / Senior / Lead
- Focus: model onboarding, evaluation, quantization profiles, and serving optimization.

5) Go-to-market (Sales, Customer Success, Growth) and Support
- Levels and compensation vary by function and are defined in GTM handbook pages.

Career growth and leveling process

- Promotion timeline: Typical minimum tenure between promotions is 12 months, but exceptional impact and documented evidence can accelerate this.
- Promotion packet: manager write-up, peer feedback, work samples (PRs, design docs, incident reviews), and a calibration review with the level committee.
- Decisions: final promotion decisions are made during the quarterly calibration cycle by the People Ops + manager + functional lead.

Benefits & perks (summary)

- Compensation: competitive base salary + equity grants; salary bands are published to managers and People Ops.
- Health & wellness: medical, dental, vision (US) or country-equivalent benefits; EAP program.
- Time off: 25 days PTO (pro-rated year 1), 10 company holidays, and flexible personal days. Parental leave: 16 weeks primary, 8 weeks secondary (paid).
- Remote / hybrid: flexible remote-first policy; monthly home office stipend ($150 USD standard, varies by country) and annual co-working allowance for hybrid employees.
- Professional development: learning stipend ($1,200/year), conference budget (team-dependent), and internal mentorship program.
- Commuter / travel: expense policy and allowances documented in Finance playbook.
- Perks: wellness reimbursements, company retreats, and complimentary access to select partner tools.

Hiring & onboarding overview

High-level hiring process
1. Requisition & job posting: Hiring manager creates a req in the ATS and partners with People Ops to publish.
2. Screening: Recruiter screens candidates for role fit and basic qualifications.
3. Interview loop: Typically includes recruiter screen, hiring manager interview, technical/assignment interview (for IC roles), and team fit interview. Interview rubrics live in team-level folders.
4. Offer: People Ops generates offers and coordinates approvals.
5. Background checks and references: run for applicable roles and jurisdictions.

New hire preboarding (before day 1)
- Checklist completed by People Ops and hiring manager:
  - Create Okta account and access groups.
  - Request GitHub org access and add to team repos.
  - Provision GCP/AWS console access with least privilege.
  - Share Welcome packet and role-specific prework.
  - Schedule first-week meetings (manager 1:1, buddy intro, security training).

First 90 days (manager & new hire checklist)
- Week 0-1:
  1) Complete security and compliance training (required).
  2) Dev environment setup: follow the Dev Quickstart (see Internal tools). Example commands:
     - git clone git@github.com:redwood/repo-name.git
     - make dev-setup
  3) Meet your buddy and 1:1 with manager to agree on 30/60/90 goals.
- Month 1:
  - Deliver a small onboarding task that touches the runtime or infra (depending on role).
  - Attend product and platform orientation sessions.
- Month 2:
  - Take ownership of a small-ticket backlog and participate in on-call shadowing if applicable.
- Month 3:
  - Present a 90-day readout to your manager and team.

Onboarding roles and responsibilities
- Hiring manager: sets expectations, schedules onboarding meetings, assigns first projects.
- Buddy: a peer-level engineer assigned for day-to-day questions and cultural context.
- People Ops: coordinates preboarding, equipment, payroll, and compliance training.
- IT/Security: provisions hardware, manages device encryption policies, and verifies MFA.

Internal tools & access guide

Core tools (what you will use and who to contact)
- Slack: primary communication. Public channels for engineering, product, and cross-functional discussion. Contact: all-hands-support@redwood.com.
- Okta: single sign-on and access management. Requests: it-support@redwood.com.
- GitHub: code hosting; teams correspond to squad names. See GitHub onboarding doc for repo-level permissions.
- Confluence: internal documentation and playbooks. This page is maintained in the company-handbook space.
- Linear: tickets and product planning (some teams use Jira; team docs specify which).
- GCP / AWS console: cloud accounts are provisioned per role with least privilege. For escalations open a ticket in the IT queue.
- Datadog / Observability: dashboards and logs for production services; SRE owns dashboards and alerting.
- Redwood Console (internal): product observability and cost dashboards for customers; access granted by product infra team.

Dev environment quickstart (example summary)
1) Request access: confirm GitHub/Okta access is provisioned.
2) Clone the monorepo and install dependencies: git clone git@github.com:redwood/infra.git && make bootstrap
3) Start local dev runtime: make dev-runtime (this will start services with local config).
4) Run tests: make test-unit && make test-integration.

Security and compliance checklist (required during onboarding)
- Complete security training within first 7 days.
- Enable MFA in Okta and register corporate device with IT.
- Sign the Data Handling and NDA agreements.
- Review the Data Residency and Retention policy if you work with customer data.

Manager guide (short)
- Set clear 30/60/90 goals within the first week.
- Schedule recurring 1:1s and weekly syncs for the first 90 days.
- Perform a formal onboarding review at 30 and 90 days and document progress in the new-hire tracker.

Offboarding (brief)
- Process owner: People Ops.
- Steps: disable Okta access, remove from GitHub teams, revoke cloud credentials, collect equipment, and perform exit interview. Full checklist in People Ops offboarding playbook.

Governance and updates
- Document ownership: People Ops maintains this page; engineering and SRE contribute role-specific ladder updates.
- Review cadence: annual review of benefits and onboarding content; role ladders reviewed quarterly during calibration.
- How to suggest changes: file a PR to this page (Confluence edit) and tag people-ops and relevant owners; for major changes request a review by the listed reviewers.

Appendices and links
- Quick links: hiring templates, interview rubrics, team ladders, benefits enrollment portal, dev quickstart, security training. See Related pages above.
- FAQ: Can I get additional budget for conferences? Yes — request via your manager and your team budget owner; approvals follow team-level process.
